body:
Footnote 26 to Paragraph 147 of ISAIF states, "... If a society needs a large
powerful law enforcement establishment, then there is something gravely wrong
with that society; it must be subjecting people to severe pressures if so many
refuse to follow the rules, or follow them only because forced. Many societies
in the past have gotten by with little or no formal law-enforcement."

In a way, this seems sensible, but I wonder about the historical reference.
Here is an example where more proof was needed. Which doesn't make the
statement wrong, just unproven. Does anyone have any examples or thoughts on
this matter?

Thanks!
